Parameter Name: LTE SAI SAC
Meaning:
SAC parameter in SAI for an SRVCC handover. The BSC interprets the handover request message as an SRVCC handover request when all the following conditions are met:
"SRVCCHOEN" in the "SET GCELLHOBASIC" command is set to YES(Yes). 
The source cell ID type in the incoming BSC handover request message is SAI.
The values of "LTE SAI MCC", "LTE SAI MNC", "LTE SAI LAC", "LTE SAI SAC" for the source cell carried in the incoming BSC handover request message are consistent with those configured on the BSC.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: LTE SAI LAC
Meaning:
LAC parameter in SAI for an SRVCC handover. The BSC interprets the handover request message as an SRVCC handover request when all the following conditions are met:
"SRVCCHOEN" in the "SET GCELLHOBASIC" command is set to YES(Yes). 
The source cell ID type in the incoming BSC handover request message is SAI.
The values of "LTE SAI MCC", "LTE SAI MNC", "LTE SAI LAC", "LTE SAI SAC" for the source cell carried in the incoming BSC handover request message are consistent with those configured on the BSC.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Intelligent Access Congest Ctrl Switch
Likely KPI Impact: CSSR / SDCCH (access delay); possible SDCCH drop
Meaning: Whether to enable the intelligent access congestion control function. When this parameter is set to ON(On), this function is enabled. The BSC dynamically adjusts the SDCCH access interval (location update) and initial uplink PS access interval to relieve network congestion. When this parameter is set to OFF(Off), this function is disabled.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to ON(On) increases the SDCCH access interval (location update) and initial uplink PS access interval and decreases the SDCCH and uplink TBF congestion rates.

Parameter Name: Intelligent Access Congest Ctrl Thres.
Likely KPI Impact: CSSR / SDCCH (access delay); possible SDCCH drop
Meaning: Threshold for triggering intelligent access congestion control. This parameter is used to check the congestion status of the location update SDCCH or uplink initial PS access.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to a small value decreases the SDCCH and uplink TBF congestion rates.

Parameter Name: Intelligent Access Congest Ctrl Timer 1
Likely KPI Impact: CSSR / SDCCH (access delay); possible SDCCH drop
Meaning:
Increased value for timer T3122. This parameter is used with "IntAcesCongCtrlThres" to dynamically specify the increase of the cell access interval. 
The BSC starts the timer specified by this parameter when an immediate assignment fails but this timer is not started. 
If the timer specified by this parameter has not expired, the increased T3122 value remains unchanged. 
If the timer specified by this parameter expires, the BSC stops the timer. If the congestion rate of SDCCH access (location update) or initial uplink PS access is greater than or equal to the value of "IntAcesCongCtrlThres" within the duration specified by the timer, the value of T3122 for SDCCH or PDCH access is incremented by 1. Otherwise, the increased T3122 value remains unchanged.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to a small value decreases the SDCCH congestion rate and uplink TBF congestion rate, but increases the location update and uplink initial PS access intervals.

Parameter Name: Intelligent Access Congest Ctrl Timer 2
Likely KPI Impact: CSSR / SDCCH (access delay); possible SDCCH drop
Meaning:
Decreased value for timer T3122. This parameter is used with "IntAcesCongCtrlThres" to dynamically specify the decrease of the cell access interval. 
The BSC automatically starts the timer specified by this parameter when the timer specified by "IntAcesCongCtrlTimer1" starts. 
If the timer specified by this parameter has not expired, the decreased T3122 value remains unchanged. 
When the timer specified by this parameter expires, if the congestion rate of SDCCH access (location update) or initial uplink PS access is less than the value of "IntAcesCongCtrlThres" within the duration specified by this timer, the value of T3122 for SDCCH access or initial uplink PS access is decreased by 1. Otherwise, the decreased T3122 value remains unchanged. 
When the decreased T3122 value is 0, the BSC stops the timer specified by this parameter. Otherwise, the BSC restarts this timer.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to a large value increases the location update interval and uplink initial PS access interval.

Likely KPI Impact: CSSR / SDCCH (access delay); possible SDCCH drop
Meaning:
Timer carried by the Wait Indication information element when the BSC sends an immediate assignment reject or DTM reject message to an MS.
After the MS receives the immediate assignment reject or DTM reject message, the MS does not reattempt to access the network until the timer expires.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, an MS is difficult to access the network. If this parameter is set to a small value, the channel load increases and the network access rate for the MS decreases.

Parameter Name: LTE SAI MCC
Meaning:
MCC parameter in SAI for an SRVCC handover. The BSC interprets the handover request message as an SRVCC handover request when all the following conditions are met:
"SRVCCHOEN" in the "SET GCELLHOBASIC" command is set to YES(Yes). 
The source cell ID type in the incoming BSC handover request message is SAI.
The values of "LTE SAI MCC", "LTE SAI MNC", "LTE SAI LAC", "LTE SAI SAC" for the source cell carried in the incoming BSC handover request message are consistent with those configured on the BSC.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: LTE SAI MNC
Meaning:
MNC parameter in SAI for an SRVCC handover. The BSC interprets the handover request message as an SRVCC handover request when all the following conditions are met:
"SRVCCHOEN" in the "SET GCELLHOBASIC" command is set to YES(Yes). 
The source cell ID type in the incoming BSC handover request message is SAI.
The values of "LTE SAI MCC", "LTE SAI MNC", "LTE SAI LAC", "LTE SAI SAC" for the source cell carried in the incoming BSC handover request message are consistent with those configured on the BSC.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Load Thld for Low Load VAMOS FR Demultiplexing
Meaning: Load threshold for triggering VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing due to low load in a common cell or in the overlaid or underlaid subcell of a concentric cell. VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing is triggered if the load in a common cell or in the overlaid or underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is less than the value of this parameter.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the later the BSC makes a decision on VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing in a common cell or in the overlaid or underlaid subcell of a concentric cell. This helps alleviate cell congestion but decreases the MOS and increases the call drop rate more significantly.

Parameter Name: Load Thres. of Channel Demultiplex
Meaning: Load threshold for triggering VAMOS HR channel demultiplexing in a common cell or in a concentric cell. VAMOS HR channel demultiplexing is triggered only when the load of a common cell or concentric cell is less than the value of this parameter.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the later the VAMOS channel demultiplexing decision due to low cell load is made, the smaller the number of times for handovers due to low cell load, the heavier the VAMOS traffic in the cell, and the greater the network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: Load Thres. in Overlaid Subcell
Meaning: Load threshold for triggering VAMOS HR channel multiplexing in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell. VAMOS HR channel multiplexing using an intra-cell handover is triggered only when the load of the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. VAMOS HR channel multiplexing using channel allocation is triggered only when the load of the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the smaller the number of new candidate VAMOS calls in the overlaid subcell. This affects VAMOS traffic volume and network quality.

Parameter Name: Channel Multiplex Load Thres.
Meaning: Load threshold for triggering VAMOS HR channel multiplexing in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell. VAMOS HR channel multiplexing using an intra-cell handover is triggered only when the load in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. VAMOS HR channel multiplexing using channel allocation is triggered only when the load in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the earlier the channel multiplexing decision is made, the higher the VAMOS traffic volume and the lower the network quality.

Parameter Name: OL Load Threshold for VAMOS FR Multiplexing
Meaning: Load threshold for triggering VAMOS FR channel multiplexing in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell. VAMOS FR channel multiplexing using an intra-cell handover is triggered only if the load in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. VAMOS FR channel multiplexing using channel allocation is triggered only if the load in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the earlier the BSC makes a decision on VAMOS FR channel multiplexing in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell and the heavier the VAMOS FR traffic in the overlaid subcell. Therefore, setting this parameter to a small value helps alleviate cell congestion. Compared with VAMOS HR, VAMOS FR has the same theoretical capacity and a higher MOS. This improves user experience. However, the HQI decreases and the call drop rate increases. Therefore, increasing the proportion of VAMOS FR deteriorates the HQI and call drop rate.

Parameter Name: Load Threshold for VAMOS FR Multiplexing
Meaning:
Load threshold for triggering VAMOS FR channel multiplexing in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell. VAMOS FR channel multiplexing using an intra-cell handover is triggered only if the load in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. 
VAMOS FR channel multiplexing using channel allocation is triggered only if the load in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the earlier the BSC makes a decision on VAMOS FR channel multiplexing in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell and the heavier the VAMOS FR traffic in the cell. Therefore, setting this parameter to a small value helps alleviate cell congestion. Compared with VAMOS HR, VAMOS FR has the same theoretical capacity and a higher MOS. This improves user experience. However, the high quality indicator (HQI) decreases and the call drop rate increases. Therefore, increasing the proportion of VAMOS FR deteriorates the HQI and call drop rate.

Parameter Name: NCC
Likely KPI Impact: HO / identity (can cause HO fail & drop)
Meaning:
Network color code that is provided by the telecom operator. The NCC is used to identify networks from area to area. Unified NCC planning is adopted by operators in a country.
The BCC and the NCC form the BSIC.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: BCC
Likely KPI Impact: HO / identity (can cause HO fail & drop)
Meaning: Base station color code (BCC) of a cell, provided by the network planning department. It is used for differentiating the cells using the same BCCH frequency. A BCC and a network color code (NCC) compose a base station identity code (BSIC).
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: RSRP Threshold for Fast FDD LTE Reselection
Meaning:
RSRP threshold for fast reselection from a GSM cell to an LTE FDD cell. The BSC sends a CHANNEL RELEASE message that carries the frequency of neighboring LTE cells only when the RSRP of the neighboring LTE cells is higher than this threshold. 
The mapping between the value of this parameter and the decibel value is as follows:
0: -140 dBm,
1: -139 dBm,
...,
63: -77dBm.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: A larger value of this parameter indicates that it is more difficult for an MS to reselect to an LTE cell. A smaller value of this parameter indicates that an MS is more likely to perform ping-pong reselections.

Parameter Name: RSRP Threshold for Fast TDD LTE Reselection
Meaning:
RSRP threshold for fast reselection from a GSM cell to an LTE TDD cell. The BSC sends the CHANNEL RELEASE message that carries the frequency of neighboring LTE cells only when the RSRP of the neighboring LTE cells is higher than this threshold. 
The mapping between the value of this parameter and the decibel value is as follows:
0: -140dBm,
1: -139dBm,
...,
63: -77dBm.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: A larger value of this parameter indicates that it is more difficult for an MS to reselect to an LTE cell. A smaller value of this parameter indicates that an MS is more likely to perform ping-pong reselections.

Parameter Name: Config Based SRVCC Fast Reselect Switch
Meaning:
Whether to allow configuration-based SRVCC fast return to LTE when MSs do not support LTE measurement.
When this parameter is set to ON, if SRVCC MSs do not support LTE frequency measurement or the BSC fails to obtain the LTE measurement capabilities of SRVCC MSs, the BSC allows SRVCC MSs to fast return to an LTE cell based on the configured LTE frequencies.
When this parameter is set to OFF, the BSC does not allow SRVCC MSs to fast return to an LTE cell based on the configured LTE frequencies.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON, configuration-based fast return to LTE can be triggered when SRVCC MSs do not support LTE frequency measurement or the BSC fails to obtain the LTE measurement capabilities of SRVCC MSs, decreasing the duration when SRVCC MSs fast return to an LTE cell. If this parameter is set to OFF, network performance is not affected.

Parameter Name: SRVCC Fast Reselect Meas Optimize Switch
Meaning:
Whether to enable the optimization of the SRVCC fast return to LTE function. 
When this parameter is set to ON:
1. If MSs support LTE frequency measurement, measurement-based fast return to LTE is triggered, and the BSC includes LTE frequencies and measurement information in the MI based on the LTE measurement capabilities of MSs.
2. If MSs do not support LTE frequency measurement or the BSC fails to obtain the LTE measurement capabilities of MSs, the BSC determines whether to trigger configuration-based fast return to LTE according to the value of the "SRVCCRapidSelBaseCfgSw" parameter. 
When this parameter is set to OFF:
1. If the "DecodeCSFBInd" parameter in the "SET AITFOTHPARA" command is set to ON(On) and the CSFB Indication IE is not carried in the Clear Command message or the value of this IE is 0, the BSC does not send the fast return message.
2. If the "DecodeCSFBInd" parameter in the "SET AITFOTHPARA" command is set to OFF(Off) or the value of the CSFB Indication IE carried in the Clear Command message is 1, the BSC sends the fast return messages to MSs based on the LTE frequency measurement results of MSs when the "FASTRETURNMEASSPT" parameter in the "SET GCELLPRIEUTRANSYS" command is set to ON(On), or sends the fast return messages to MSs based on the LTE frequencies for which the "SPTRAPIDSEL" parameter in the "ADD GLTENCELL" or "MOD GLTENCELL" command is set to SUPPORT when the "FASTRETURNMEASSPT" parameter in the "SET GCELLPRIEUTRANSYS" command is set to OFF(Off).
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON, the BSC sends more accurate LTE frequencies to MSs based on MS capabilities, and MSs measure LTE frequencies more accurately and return to an LTE cell more quickly. If this parameter is set to OFF, network performance is not affected.

Parameter Name: Concentric Intelligent Shutdown Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the intelligent power saving optimization function in a concentric cell. When this parameter is set to ON, power amplifier of the TRX serving the overlaid subcell is shut down when the cell traffic is light; the traffic will be carried by the TRX serving the underlaid subcell to obtain maximum power saving gains. When this parameter is set to OFF, power amplifier of the TRX serving the overlaid subcell is shut down only when all traffic of the overlaid subcell is released.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to ON increases traffic carried by the underlaid subcell.

Parameter Name: Allow Dynamic Shutdown of TRX
Meaning: This parameter specifies whether to allow the BSC to enable the TRX Intelligent Shutdown feature on a cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Energy Conserve Prefer Switch
Meaning: Whether the BSC preferentially allocates channels on a power amplifier-enabled TRX when an MS attempts to perform voice services. If this parameter is set to ON, within the power saving period specified in the "SET BSCDSTPA" command, power saving takes precedence over capacity and quality during channel allocation, and the BSC preferentially allocates channels on a power amplifier-enabled TRX during a call access or handover. If this parameter is set to OFF, the BSC does not preferentially allocate channels on a power amplifier-enabled TRX; instead, it allocates channels based on the policy specified by the "CHALLOCSTRATEGY" parameter in the "SET GCELLCHMGBASIC" command.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: PDCH TRX Intelligent Shutdown Switch
Meaning: Whether to allow shutdown of TRXs with PDCHs in the TRX Power Amplifier Intelligent Shutdown feature. When this parameter is set to ENABLED, users can set "CPS" in "SET GTRXDEV" to YES for TRXs with static PDCHs, and TRXs with PDCHs support intelligent power amplifier shutdown. When this parameter is set to DISABLED, users cannot set "CPS" in "SET GTRXDEV" to YES for TRXs with static PDCHs, and TRXs with PDCHs do not support intelligent power amplifier shutdown.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Enabling this function helps conserve power but decreases PS capacity.

Parameter Name: Allow HO Multiplex Before CONNECT ACK
Meaning:
Whether to allow VAMOS multiplexing for an MS that has not received a Connect ACK message. 
When this parameter is set to ON, VAMOS multiplexing is allowed for such an MS.
When this parameter is set to OFF, VAMOS multiplexing is not allowed for such an MS.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to OFF, the VAMOS multiplexing rate decreases. If this parameter is set to ON, the call drop rate after VAMOS multiplexing increases.

Parameter Name: Mute SAIC Terminal Processing Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the function for processing mute SAIC-capable MSs in a cell. A mute SAIC-capable MS is a SAIC-capable MS that is reported as SAIC-incapable. The value ON indicates that the function for processing such MSs is enabled; the value OFF indicates that the function for processing such MSs is disabled. Processing mute SAIC-capable MSs consists of identification of such MSs based on database records and automatic identification of such MSs.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When this parameter is set to ON, IMEI identification is performed before the BSC assigns a TCH, delaying call access.

Parameter Name: Problem SAIC Terminal Processing Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the function for processing SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects in a cell. The value ON indicates that the function for processing such MSs is enabled; the value OFF indicates that the function for processing such MSs is disabled. Processing SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects consists of identification of such MSs based on database records and automatic identification of such MSs.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When this parameter is set to ON, IMEI identification is performed before the BSC assigns the TCH, delaying call access.

Parameter Name: DL Rx Qual. Thres. of Established Calls
Meaning:
Threshold of the downlink receive quality of an established call to be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. The decision on this call can be triggered successfully only when the following conditions are met: 1. The ATCB of this call is greater than or equal to the ATCB threshold. 2. The uplink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd". 3. The downlink receive quality is smaller than or equal to the value of this parameter. 4. The uplink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd". 5. The downlink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd". 6. The absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels is less than or equal to "VamosAntUlRxlevDiffThd".
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the smaller the number of accessed candidate VAMOS calls. As a result, VAMOS traffic volume decreases and network quality deteriorates slightly.

Parameter Name: DL Rx Lev. Thres. of VAMOS Calls
Meaning:
Threshold of the downlink receive level of an established call to be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. VAMOS is short for voice services over adaptive multi-user channels on one slot. The decision on an established call can be triggered successfully only when both of the following conditions are met: 1. The downlink receive level of an established call is greater than or equal to this threshold. 2. The uplink and downlink receive quality, uplink and downlink receive levels, ATCB, and absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels meet relevant requirements. 
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the smaller the number of new candidate VAMOS calls. This affects VAMOS traffic volume and network quality.

Parameter Name: UL Rx Qual. Thres. of Established Calls
Meaning:
Threshold of the uplink receive quality of an established call to be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. The decision on this call can be triggered successfully only when all of the following conditions are met: 1. The ATCB of this call is greater than or equal to the ATCB threshold. 2. The uplink receive quality is smaller than or equal to the value of this parameter. 3. The downlink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd". 4. The uplink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd". 5. The downlink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd". 6. The absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels is less than or equal to "VamosAntUlRxlevDiffThd".
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a small value, the number of established calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: UL RX Level Thld for Channel Multiplexing
Meaning: Uplink receive level threshold for a call that has accessed a cell to serve as a candidate VAMOS call. This parameter works with "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT", and "VFRRxlevOffset" to specify the uplink receive level standard of a candidate VAMOS call. An accessed call whose uplink receive level fails to meet the standard cannot serve as a candidate VAMOS call. The preceding rule is invalid if this parameter is set to 0.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the higher the required uplink receive level of a candidate VAMOS call, the less the candidate VAMOS calls, and the lower the VAMOS traffic volume.

Parameter Name: Allow VAMOS-1&NonSAIC and SAIC&NonSAIC
Meaning: Whether to allow the multiplexing of a VAMOS-1 call and a non-SAIC call and the multiplexing of a SAIC call and a non-SAIC call. The value ON indicates that the two types of multiplexing are allowed; the value OFF indicates that the two types of multiplexing are not allowed.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON(On), the VAMOS channel multiplexing rate and network capacity  increase. However, network quality deteriorates noticeably after the preceding pairs of calls are multiplexed because of poor link performance.

Parameter Name: DL RX Level Thd of Terminal Identify
Meaning: Threshold of downlink receive level for triggering automatic identification of mute SAIC MSs and problem SAIC MSs. When the downlink receive level of a call is lower than the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is not performed. The preceding rule is invalid if this parameter is set to 0.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a larger value, the required downlink receive level for triggering automatic identification is larger. Therefore, automatic identification is performed on fewer calls in the network. As a result, fewer calls are affected and network quality decreases at a slower rate. However, the automatic identification efficiency is lower.

Parameter Name: LO Thresh upon Terminal Identify Request
Meaning: Load threshold for performing automatic identification of mute SAIC-capable MSs, SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects, and SAIC white MSs in a cell. MS identification request is triggered only when cell load is lower than or equal to the value of this parameter.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, mute SAIC terminal identification is triggered in a cell with high load. The number of automatic identification decisions made by MSs increases and network quality deteriorates seriously.

Parameter Name: Max Calls in Terminal Identification
Meaning: Maximum number of calls in a cell, on which identification of mute SAIC-capable MSs, identification of SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects, and identification of SAIC white MSs can be performed simultaneously.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, automatic mute SAIC terminal identification and problem SAIC terminal identification can be performed simultaneously on more calls in a cell. Therefore, the number of calls affected by the identification process increases and network quality deteriorates seriously.

Parameter Name: UL RX Level Thd of Terminal Identify
Meaning: Threshold of uplink receive level for triggering automatic identification of mute SAIC MSs and problem SAIC MSs. When the uplink receive level of a call is lower than the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is not performed. The preceding rule is invalid if this parameter is set to 0.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a larger value, the required uplink receive level for triggering automatic identification is larger. Therefore, automatic identification is performed on fewer calls in the network. As a result, fewer calls are affected and network quality decreases at a slower rate. However, the automatic identification efficiency is lower.

Parameter Name: Channel Multiplex Rx Qual. Thres. Offset in Asgmt.
Meaning: Offset of the uplink or downlink receive quality of a new call against the quality threshold of existing calls. If a new call is to be selected as a candidate call for VAMOS channel multiplexing during channel assignment, its uplink receive quality must be smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset" and its downlink receive quality must be smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of new calls as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases. If this parameter is set to a small value, the number of new calls as VAMOS candidate calls increases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell increases, and the deterioration of network quality increases.

Parameter Name: Enable BQ VAMOS Channel Demultiplex Penalty
Meaning: Whether to enable the BQ VAMOS demultiplexing penalty function. If this parameter is set to ON, the BSC, after performing VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to BQ on a pair of multiplexed calls, performs penalty on the call with poorer quality. In this case, the BSC forbids VAMOS channel multiplexing on the call. If this parameter is set to OFF, the BSC does not perform penalty on the call with poorer quality.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON, the call drop rate decreases, but the VAMOS traffic volume also decreases.

Parameter Name: Primary TSC in VAMOS
Meaning: Primary Training Sequence Code (TSC) used in the network when the VAMOS function is enabled in a cell. Before all calls enter the VAMOS mode, the primary TSC is assigned preferentially; after a pair of VAMOS calls is multiplexed, the TSC that is not used by the call that accesses the timeslot first is assigned to the other call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Secondary TSC in VAMOS
Meaning: Secondary Training Sequence Code (TSC) used in the network when the VAMOS function is enabled in a cell. Before all calls enter the VAMOS mode, the primary TSC is assigned preferentially; after a pair of VAMOS calls is multiplexed, the TSC that is not used by the call that accesses the timeslot first is assigned to the other call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Opt VAMOS Channel Multiplexing Alg Allowed
Meaning: Whether to use the optimized VAMOS channel multiplexing algorithm. When this parameter is set to YES, all MSs in the candidate VAMOS call queue are sorted in ascending order of receive quality of established candidate calls. MSs with the same receive quality are sorted in descending order of ATCB. When this parameter is set to NO, all MSs in the candidate VAMOS call queue are sorted in ascending order of path loss of established candidate calls.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When this parameter is set to YES, the speech quality does not deteriorate or improves. This algorithm will significantly improve the speech quality if the VAMOS and IBCA functions are enabled together.

Parameter Name: SAIC White MS Identification Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the SAIC white MS identification function. An SAIC white MS refers to a SAIC MS that supports Alpha-QPSK modulation. If this parameter is set to ON, this function is enabled, and the BSC identifies SAIC white MSs and can use Alpha-QPSK modulation on the multiplexed SAIC white MSs in the downlink. If this parameter is set to OFF, this function is disabled.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON, the BSC identifies SAIC white MSs, the VAMOS multiplexing performance improves, but the call drop rate increases and the voice quality deteriorates.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thres of Terminal Identify
Meaning: ATCB threshold of a call for triggering automatic MS identification. When the ATCB of a call is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter, automatic identification of mute SAIC-capable MSs and SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects is performed. The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 64.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the ATCB of a call in terminal identification request is high, and terminal identification can be performed on few calls. This eases network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: DL RX Qual Thres of Terminal Identify
Meaning: Threshold of the downlink receive quality of a call for triggering automatic MS identification.When the downlink receive quality of a call is greater than the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is not performed. When the downlink receive quality of a call is lower than or equal to the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is performed.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a small value, automatic mute SAIC terminal identification is performed on calls with favorable downlink receive quality. Therefore, automatic mute SAIC terminal identification is performed on few calls in the network. As a result, few calls are affected and network quality decreases slightly.

Parameter Name: Satisfy Time for Terminal Identify
Meaning: Duration in which uplink and downlink quality, uplink and downlink levels, and ATCB of a call meet the thresholds. If the duration in which uplink and downlink quality,uplink and downlink levels, and ATCB of a call meet the thresholds within the time specified by "SpeMsIdeStatTimes" is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter, MS identification is allowed to be triggered.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, a longer period of observing uplink and downlink call quality and ATCB for triggering automatic identification is required. In this case, the BSC triggers MS identification at a later time, thereby decreasing the number of calls on which MS identification can be performed on the network. As a result, the number of calls affected by MS identification decreases, and network quality deteriorates more slightly.

Parameter Name: Watch Time for Terminal Identify
Meaning: Observation period for uplink and downlink quality, uplink and downlink levels, ATCB of a call. If the duration in which uplink and downlink quality,uplink and downlink levels, and ATCB of a call meet the thresholds within the time specified by this parameter is greater than or equal to the value of "SpeMsIdeLastTimes", MS identification is allowed to be triggered.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, a long period for observing uplink and downlink call quality and ATCB is required. Therefore, automatic terminal identification is triggered late and few calls are affected, which deteriorates network quality slightly.

Parameter Name: UL RX Qual Thres of Terminal Identify
Meaning: Threshold of the uplink receive quality of a call for triggering automatic identification of mute SAIC-capable MSs and SAIC-capable MSs with AFC defects. When the uplink receive quality of a call is greater than the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is not performed. When the uplink receive quality of a call is lower than or equal to the value of this parameter, automatic identification of such MSs is performed.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a small value, automatic mute SAIC terminal identification is performed on calls with favorable uplink receive quality. Therefore, automatic mute SAIC terminal identification is performed on few calls in the network. As a result, few calls are affected and network quality deteriorates less.

Parameter Name: Main and Diversity UL RX Level Diff Thld for MUX
Meaning: Uplink main and diversity receive level difference threshold for candidate VAMOS call decision. If the main and diversity receive level difference after measurement report filtering is greater than the value of this parameter, VAMOS multiplexing is not allowed. The preceding rule is invalid if this parameter is set to 127.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to an overly large value, calls with overly large main and diversity receive level differences can receive VAMOS multiplexing. As a result, the uplink HQIs and call drop rate deteriorate. If this parameter is set to an overly small value, calls with proper main and diversity receive level differences cannot receive VAMOS multiplexing. As a result, the VAMOS traffic volume decreases and network congestion becomes more severe.

Parameter Name: Rx Lev. Thres. Offset During Assignment
Meaning: Offset of the downlink receive level of a new call from the level threshold of established calls if the new call is to be selected as a VAMOS candidate call during assignment. A new call can be selected as a VAMOS candidate call only when the following conditions are met: The downlink receive level of the new call is greater than or equal to the sum of DL Rx Lev. Thres. of VAMOS Calls and this parameter. The uplink and downlink receive quality as well as the ATCB meet relevant requirements.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the smaller the number of new candidate VAMOS calls. This affects VAMOS traffic volume and network quality.

Parameter Name: Multiplexing Load Thres. Offset in Assignment
Meaning: Offset between the load threshold and the handover multiplexing load threshold for VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment. When VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is enabled in common cells and underlaid subcells in concentric cells, the decision procedure for VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is triggered if the cell load or load in the underlaid subcell is higher than or equal to the sum of "VamosMultLoadThd" and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT". When VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is enabled in overlaid subcells, the decision procedure for VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is triggered if the load in the overlaid subcell is higher than or equal to the sum of "VamosIuoInnerLoadThd" and "VAMOSASSLOADOFT". The actual value for this parameter is the GUI value for this parameter minus 100.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the lower the load start threshold required by VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment, the earlier the VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is triggered.

Parameter Name: Channel Multiplex ATCB Thres. Offset in Asgmt.
Meaning: Offset of the ATCB for a new call from the ATCB threshold for existing calls, if the new call is to be selected as a candidate VAMOS HR call during channel allocation. If the new call is a Non-SAIC call in a common cell or in the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the ATCB for the new call must be greater than or equal to the sum of the values of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd" and "VamosAssMultAtcbOffset". If the new call is a Non-SAIC call in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the ATCB for the new call must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd", "VamosAssMultAtcbOffset", and "VamosIuoInnerAtcbThd". The preceding rules apply to SAIC calls, VAMOS I calls, and VAMOS II calls that are newly set up.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of new calls as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: Allow Channel Multiplex in Assignment
Meaning: Whether to enable VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment in the network. The value ON indicates that VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is enabled in a cell; the value OFF indicates that VAMOS channel multiplexing during assignment is disabled in a cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When "VamosSwitch" is set to ON, VFR, or VHR and "VamosAssSwitch" is set to ON, the network congestion rate decreases significantly; however, network quality decreases after VAMOS calls are multiplexed.

Parameter Name: OL BQ Demultiplexing Rx Quality Thres. Offset
Meaning:
Receive signal quality threshold offset between a VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell and a VAMOS call in the underlaid subcell during channel demultiplexing due to bad quality. VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to bad quality is triggered if the P/N criterion is met and either of the following conditions is met:
The uplink receive signal quality of the VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell is higher than or equal to "VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT". The downlink receive signal quality of the VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell is higher than or equal to "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT". 
The actual value for this parameter is the GUI value for this parameter minus 70.
Impact on Radio Network Performance:
The smaller the value of this parameter:
The smaller the receive signal quality offset between a VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell and a VAMOS call in the underlaid subcell during channel demultiplexing due to bad quality
The later the channel demultiplexing due to bad quality is triggered
The more the VAMOS traffic volume
The lower the network quality.

Parameter Name: VAMOS FACCH Send Enhance Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the VAMOS FACCH send enhance function. Setting this parameter to ON automatically converts Alpha-QPSK modulation to GMSK modulation for the FACCH when the quality of the radio environment is poor. Therefore, downlink FACCH demodulation performance can be improved significantly.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to ON decreases the VAMOS call drop rate but may also slightly decrease the MOS of multiplexed calls.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thres. of Established Non-SAIC Calls
Meaning: ATCB threshold of an established non-SAIC call to be selected as a candidate call for VAMOS channel multiplexing. The decision on an established Non-SAIC call can be triggered successfully only when the following conditions are met: The ATCB of the call is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. The uplink receive quality is lower than or equal to "UL Rx Qual. Thres. of Established Calls". The downlink receive quality is lower than or equal to "DL Rx Qual. Thres. of Established Calls". If the decision conditions are met for "Duration of Satisfying Candidate VAMOS Call" within "Watch Time of Candidate Calls", this call can be selected as a VAMOS candidate call. The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 64.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of established Non-SAIC calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thres. of Established SAIC Calls
Meaning:
ATCB threshold of an established SAIC call to be selected as a candidate call for VAMOS channel multiplexing. The decision on an established SAIC call can be triggered successfully only when all of the following conditions are met: 1. The ATCB of the call is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. 2. The uplink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd". 3. The downlink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd". 
4. The uplink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd". 5. The downlink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd". 6. The absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels is less than or equal to "VamosAntUlRxlevDiffThd".
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 64.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of established SAIC calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: Allow Channel Multiplex via In-Cell HO
Meaning: Whether to enable VAMOS channel multiplexing through intra-cell handover in the network. The value ON indicates that VAMOS channel multiplexing through intra-cell handover is enabled in a cell; the value OFF indicates that VAMOS channel multiplexing through intra-cell handover is disabled in a cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When "VamosSwitch" is set to ON, VFR, or VHR and "VamosAssSwitch" is set to ON, the network congestion rate decreases significantly; however, network quality decreases after VAMOS calls are multiplexed.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thres. of Established VAMOS-1 Calls
Meaning:
ATCB threshold of an established VAMOS-1 call to be selected as a candidate call for VAMOS HR channel multiplexing. The decision on an established VAMOS-1 call can be triggered successfully only when all of the following conditions are met: 1. The ATCB of the call is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. 2. The uplink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd". 3. The downlink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd". 
4. The uplink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd". 5. The downlink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd". 6. The absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels is less than or equal to "VamosAntUlRxlevDiffThd".
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 64.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of established VAMOS-1 calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thres. of Established VAMOS-2 Calls
Meaning:
ATCB threshold of an established VAMOS-2 call to be selected as a candidate call for VAMOS channel multiplexing. The decision on an established VAMOS-2 call can be triggered successfully only when all of the following conditions are met: 1. The ATCB of the call is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter. 2. The uplink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd". 3. The downlink receive quality is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd". 
4. The uplink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd". 5. The downlink receive level is greater than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd". 6. The absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels is less than or equal to "VamosAntUlRxlevDiffThd".
If the decision conditions are met for "VamosOldCallLastTimes" within "VamosOldCallStatTimes", this call can be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. Otherwise, this call cannot be selected as a candidate VAMOS call. The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 64.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the number of established VAMOS-2 calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases, the VAMOS traffic volume in the cell decreases, and the deterioration of network quality eases.

Parameter Name: ATCB Offset in Overlaid Subcell
Meaning: Offset of the ATCB of a new call in the overlaid subcell from the ATCB threshold of a new call in the underlaid subcell if the new call in the overlaid subcell is to be selected as a VAMOS candidate call during assignment.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the smaller the number of new candidate VAMOS calls in the overlaid subcell. This affects VAMOS traffic volume and network quality.

Parameter Name: Channel Demultiplex on Low Cell Load
Meaning: Whether to enable VAMOS channel demultiplexing when the load in a cell is low. The value ON indicates that VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to low cell load is enabled; the value OFF indicates that VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to low cell load is disabled.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When this parameter is set to ON and "VamosSwitch" is set to ON, VFR, or VHR, KPIs related to network quality improve.

Parameter Name: MS Support VAMOS I&II Enable
Meaning: Whether to support VAMOS I and II MSs. The VAMOS performance of VAMOS I and VAMOS II MSs is better than that of SAIC-capable MSs. If this parameter is set to ON, the BSS supports VAMOS I and VAMOS II MSs.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Setting this parameter to ON can improve the VAMOS performance of a network.

Parameter Name: VAMOS No DL MR Handover Optimize Switch
Meaning: Whether to optimize handovers due to no downlink measurement report (MR) for VAMOS calls. If this parameter is set to ON, the BSC preferentially performs handovers due to no downlink MR in a cell for VAMOS calls when the conditions for performing handovers due to no downlink MR are met. In addition, such handovers are not controlled by [GCELLHOEMG:NODLMRHOEN] and [GCELLHOBASIC:INTRACELLHOEN]. If this parameter is set to OFF, the BSC does not optimize handovers due to no downlink MR for VAMOS calls, and such handovers are controlled by [GCELLHOEMG:NODLMRHOEN].
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Duration of Satisfying Candidate VAMOS Call
Meaning: Duration within which a call satisfies the decision conditions for selecting a VAMOS candidate call. If the decision conditions are met for "Duration of Satisfying Candidate VAMOS Call" within "Watch Time of Candidate Calls". Otherwise, this call can be selected as a VAMOS candidate call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the decision of accepting a call as a VAMOS candidate call is triggered late, and the number of calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases. These affect the number of VAMOS candidate calls and timeliness of VAMOS channel multiplexing.

Parameter Name: Watch Time of Candidate Calls
Meaning: Duration within which the ATCB and receive quality of a call are observed to determine whether this call can be selected as a VAMOS candidate call. If the decision is triggered for "Duration of Satisfying Candidate VAMOS Call" within the period of time specified by this parameter. Otherwise, this call can be selected as a VAMOS candidate call.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, the decision of accepting a call as a VAMOS candidate call is triggered late, and the number of calls that can be selected as VAMOS candidate calls decreases. These affect the number of VAMOS candidate calls and timeliness of VAMOS channel multiplexing.

Parameter Name: OL Multiplexing Rx Level Thres. Offset
Meaning:
Receive level threshold offset between a call in the overlaid subcell and a call in the underlaid subcell when a call is selected as the candidate VAMOS call during channel multiplexing in the overlaid subcell. A new call in the overlaid subcell is selected as the candidate VAMOS call if all of the following conditions are met: 1. The downlink receive level of the new call is greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset" and "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT". 2. The uplink receive level of the new call is greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", and "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT". 3. The uplink and downlink receive quality, ATCB, absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels, and P/N criterion meets relevant requirements. 
An established call in the overlaid subcell is selected as the candidate VAMOS call if both of the following conditions are met: 1. The downlink receive level of the established call is greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd" and "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT". 2. The uplink and downlink receive quality, ATCB, absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels, and P/N criterion meets relevant requirements.
The actual value for this parameter is the GUI value for this parameter minus 128.
Impact on Radio Network Performance:
The smaller the value of this parameter:
The smaller the receive signal level offset between a call in the overlaid subcell that regards as the candidate VAMOS call and a call in the underlaid subcell that regards as the candidate VAMOS call
The looser the conditions for selecting a call as the candidate VAMOS call
The more the VAMOS traffic volume
The lower the network quality.

Parameter Name: OL Multiplexing Rx Quality Thres. Offset
Meaning:
Receive quality offset between a call in the overlaid subcell and a call in the underlaid subcell when decisions on candidate VAMOS calls are made during VAMOS channel multiplexing in the overlaid subcell. A new call in the overlaid subcell can be used as the candidate VAMOS call if all of the following conditions are met: 1. The uplink receive quality of the new call is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset" and "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT". 2. The downlink receive quality of the new call is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset" and "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT". 3. The uplink and downlink receive levels, ATCB, absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels, and P/N criterion meet relevant requirements. 
An established call in the overlaid subcell can be used as the candidate VAMOS call if all of the following conditions are met: 1. The uplink receive quality of the established call is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" minus "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT". 2. The downlink receive quality of the established call is smaller than or equal to "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" minus "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT". 3. The uplink and downlink receive levels, ATCB, absolute value of the difference between main and diversity receive levels, and P/N criterion meet relevant requirements. 
The actual value of this parameter equals the GUI value minus 70.
Impact on Radio Network Performance:
The smaller the value of this parameter:
The smaller the receive signal level offset between a call in the overlaid subcell that regards as the candidate VAMOS call and a call in the underlaid subcell that regards as the candidate VAMOS call
The looser the conditions for selecting a call as the candidate VAMOS call
The more the VAMOS traffic volume
The lower the network quality.

Parameter Name: Path Loss Offset Thres. of VAMOS Call
Meaning: Threshold of the absolute value of the path loss difference between two calls for VAMOS channel multiplexing. When the absolute value of the path loss difference between two calls is smaller than or equal to this threshold, the two calls are allowed to be multiplexed.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the more VAMOS calls and the less multiplexing attempts. This affects VAMOS traffic volume and network quality.

Parameter Name: DL RX Bad Qual. Demultiplex Thres.
Meaning: Downlink receive quality threshold of a VAMOS call in channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality in a cell. The decision of channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality is triggered when either of the following conditions is met: 1. The downlink receive quality of a VAMOS call in a common cell or underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to this threshold or the uplink receive quality is greater than or equal to " VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd". 2. The downlink receive quality of a VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT" or the uplink receive quality is greater than or equal to the value of "VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT". A call can be demultiplexed using the intra-cell handover only when the decision conditions are met for times specified by "VamosQualReuseLastTimes" within the duration specified by "VamosQualReuseStatTimes".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the later VAMOS channel demultiplexing decision is made due to poor call quality, the smaller the number of times for handovers due to poor call quality, the heavier the VAMOS traffic in the cell, and the greater the network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: Bad Qual. Duration for Demultiplex
Meaning: Duration in which a call satisfies the conditions for channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality in a cell. Within "Watch Time of Poor Qual. for Demultiplex", a call can be demultiplexed only when it satisfies the conditions for "Poor Qual. Duration for Demultiplex".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the later the VAMOS channel multiplexing decision is made due to poor call quality, the heavier the VAMOS traffic in the cell, and the greater the network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: Watch Time of Bad Qual. for Demultiplex
Meaning: Duration for observing the receive quality of a VAMOS call in the decision of channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality in a cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the later the VAMOS channel multiplexing decision is made due to poor call quality, the heavier the VAMOS traffic in the cell, and the greater the network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: Channel Demultiplex on Bad Qual.
Meaning: Whether to enable VAMOS channel demultiplexing when the speech quality of a call is poor. The value ON indicates that VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality is enabled; the value OFF indicates that VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality is disabled.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: When this parameter is set to ON and "VamosSwitch" is set to ON, VFR, or VHR, KPIs related to network quality improve.

Parameter Name: UL RX Bad Qual. Demultiplex Thres.
Meaning: Uplink receive quality threshold of a VAMOS call in channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality in a cell. The decision of channel demultiplexing due to poor speech quality is triggered when either of the following conditions is met: 1. The uplink receive quality of a VAMOS call in a common cell or underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to this threshold or the downlink receive quality is greater than or equal to "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd". 2. The uplink receive quality of a VAMOS call in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the value of "VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT" or the downlink receive quality is greater than or equal to "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT". A call can be demultiplexed using the intra-cell handover only when the decision conditions are met for times specified by "VamosQualReuseLastTimes" within the duration specified by "VamosQualReuseStatTimes".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the later VAMOS channel demultiplexing decision is made due to poor call quality, the smaller the number of times for handovers due to poor call quality, the heavier the VAMOS traffic in the cell, and the greater the network quality deterioration.

Parameter Name: BQ VAMOS Channel Demultiplex Optimize
Meaning: Whether to optimize bad quality (BQ) VAMOS channel demultiplexing handovers. If this parameter is set to ON, quality-based handovers (interference, BQ and TCHF-to-TCHH handover) except BQ VAMOS channel demultiplexing handovers are not allowed for VAMOS calls. During such a handover, a call with good signal quality is handed over to another channel, whereas a call with poor signal quality cannot be handed over through any quality-based handovers during the penalty period specified by "BQ VAMOS Channel Demultiplex Penalty Period".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to ON, only BQ VAMOS channel demultiplexing handovers among quality-based handovers are allowed for VAMOS calls. During a BQ VAMOS channel demultiplexing handover, a call with good signal quality is handed over to another channel. This increases the success rate for BQ VAMOS channel demultiplexing handovers and decreases the VAMOS call drop rate.

Parameter Name: BQ VAMOS Channel Demultiplex Penalty Period
Meaning: When VAMOS channel demultiplexing due to BQ is performed, a call with good signal quality is handed over to another channel, whereas a call with poor signal quality cannot be handed over through any quality-based handovers (interference, BQ, or TCHF/TCHH handovers). This parameter specifies the period during which quality-based handovers or VAMOS multiplexing cannot be performed on a call with poor signal quality.
Impact on Radio Network Performance:
If this parameter is set to an overly large value: When "VamosBQDemuxPenSw" is set to OFF(Off), the number of call drops due to BQ increases, and voice quality deteriorates. When "VamosBQDemuxPenSw" is set to ON(On), VAMOS traffic decreases.
If this parameter is set to an overly small value: When "VamosBQDemuxPenSw" is set to OFF(Off), handovers are frequently performed, and the signaling load increases. When "VamosBQDemuxPenSw" is set to ON(On), the number of call drops due to VAMOS multiplexing increases.

Parameter Name: VAMOS Switch
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The VAMOS function increases network capacity by sacrificing quality. As a result, when the VAMOS function is enabled, the network capacity increases and the congestion rate decreases; however, the quality-related network KPIs deteriorate.

Parameter Name: VAMOS TSC Automatic Mapping Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the VAMOS TSC automatic mapping function. When this parameter is set to ON, the frequency hopping (FH) group training sequence code (TSC) serves as the primary TSC used by VAMOS multiplexing calls in FH mode, and the base station color code (BCC) serves as the primary TSC used by VAMOS multiplexing calls in non-FH mode. The secondary TSC in VAMOS is obtained based on its mapping relationship with the primary TSC in VAMOS. When this parameter is set to OFF, the primary and secondary TSCs used by VAMOS multiplexing calls are controlled by "VamosMainTsc" and "VamosSubTsc".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The values of S3281:Maximum Distance Between MS and BTS and AS3280:Mean Distance Between MS and BTS change, and the high quality indicator (HQI) may slightly decrease.

Parameter Name: ATCB Thld Offset for VAMOS FR Multiplexing
Meaning: ATCB threshold offset of the decision on candidate VAMOS FR calls from that on candidate VAMOS HR calls. The adaptive cell border (ATCB) of a non-Single Antenna Interference Cancellation (SAIC) MS that newly accesses a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd", "VamosAssMultAtcbOffset", and this parameter. The ATCB of a non-SAIC MS that has accessed a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd" and this parameter. The ATCB of a non-SAIC MS that newly accesses the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell must be greater than equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd", "VamosAssMultAtcbOffset", "VamosIuoInnerAtcbThd", and this parameter. The ATCB of a non-SAIC MS that has accessed the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoNoneSaicAtcbThd", "VamosIuoInnerAtcbThd", and this parameter. The preceding rules apply to SAIC MSs, VAMOS I MSs, and VAMOS II MSs. The actual value of this parameter equals to the current value of this parameter minus 64. If this parameter is set to a value less than 64, the actual value is a negative value.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the higher the ATCB of a candidate VAMOS FR call, the fewer the candidate VAMOS FR calls that meet the requirement, and the lighter the VAMOS FR traffic, decreasing the HQI and increasing the call drop rate less significantly.

Parameter Name: RX Quality Thld Offset for VAMOS FR Multiplex
Recommended Value: 5(to further increase the VAMOS FR traffic volume without affecting the VAMOS HR traffic volume)
Meaning:
Receive quality threshold offset for the decision on candidate VAMOS FR calls. For a call that newly accesses a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset"; and the downlink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" minus "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset". 
For a call that has accessed a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd"; and the downlink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd".
For a call that newly accesses the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and the result of ("VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" - "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset" - "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT"); and the downlink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and the result of ("VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" - "VamosAssUlQualThdOffset" - "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT").
For a call that has accessed the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoUlQualThd" minus "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT"; and the downlink receive quality must be less than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosIntraHoDlQualThd" minus "VAMOSOLRXQUALOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the higher the requirement on the receive quality of a candidate VAMOS FR call, the fewer the candidate VAMOS FR calls that meet the requirement, and the lighter the VAMOS FR traffic, decreasing the HQI and increasing the call drop rate less significantly.

Parameter Name: RX Quality Thld Offset for BQ FR Demultiplexing
Recommended Value: 5(to further increase the VAMOS FR traffic volume without affecting the VAMOS HR traffic volume)
Meaning:
Receive quality threshold offset for triggering VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing due to bad quality. VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing due to bad quality is triggered if one of the following conditions is met:
1. The uplink receive quality of a VAMOS FR call in a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd" and this parameter. 
2. The downlink receive quality of this call is greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd" and this parameter. 
3. The uplink receive quality of a VAMOS FR call in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosQualReuseUpLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT".
4. The downlink receive quality of a VAMOS FR call in the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell is greater than or equal to the sum of this parameter and "VamosQualReuseDownLinkQualThd" minus "VAMOSDEPOLRXQUALOFT".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The smaller the value of this parameter, the earlier the BSC triggers the decision on VAMOS FR channel demultiplexing due to uplink/downlink bad quality, and the lighter the VAMOS FR traffic. In addition, the MOS decreases and the call drop rate increases less significantly.

Parameter Name: RX Level Thld Offset for VAMOS FR Multiplexing
Meaning:
Receive level threshold offset for the decision on candidate VAMOS FR calls. For a call that newly accesses a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", and this parameter; and the downlink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", and this parameter. 
For a call that has accessed a common cell or the underlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd" and this parameter; and the downlink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd" and this parameter. 
For a call that newly accesses the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT", and this parameter; and the downlink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd", "VamosAssDlRxlevThdOffset", "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT", and this parameter.
For a call that has accessed the overlaid subcell of a concentric cell, the uplink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoUlRxlevThd", "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT", and this parameter; and the downlink receive level must be greater than or equal to the sum of "VamosIntraHoDlRxlevThd", "VAMOSOLRXLEVOFT", and this parameter. 
The actual value of this parameter equals to the current value of this parameter minus 128. If this parameter is set to a value less than 128, the actual value is a negative value.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The larger the value of this parameter, the higher the requirement on the downlink receive level of a candidate VAMOS FR call, the fewer the candidate VAMOS FR calls that meet the requirement, and the lighter the VAMOS FR traffic, decreasing the HQI and increasing the call drop rate less significantly.

Parameter Name: Enable VAMOS FR to HR Multiplexing Conversion
Meaning: Whether to allow the conversion from a VAMOS FR call to a VAMOS HR call when the network load is heavier than "VamosMultLoadThd".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Converting VAMOS FR calls to VAMOS HR calls increases the usage efficiency of radio resources but increases call drop risks. Setting this parameter to ON decreases the VAMOS FR traffic volume and MOS, increases the VAMOS HR traffic volume, and alleviates network congestion.

Parameter Name: TCH Traffic Busy Threshold
Meaning: If the current channel seizure ratio reaches or exceeds this value, the half-rate TCH is assigned preferentially; otherwise, the full-rate TCH is assigned preferentially.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, congestion occurs in the cell during peak hours. If this parameter is set to a small value, TCHHs are allocated to MSs even if the cell load is light, deteriorating the voice quality.

Parameter Name: AMR TCH/H Prior Cell Load Threshold
Meaning: Load threshold for assigning half rate channels preferentially. If the current TCH seizure ratio of the cell is greater than or equal to this threshold, AMR half rate channels are assigned preferentially.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, cell congestion cannot be relieved. If this parameter is set to a small value, TCHHs are assigned unnecessarily, affecting the voice quality.

Parameter Name: Level Thresh for Assign BCCH Under TBCCH
Meaning:
During channel assignment, the assignment of channels on the BCCH TRXs depends on the uplink receive level, quality, and non-BCCH load. The TCHs are preferentially assigned on the BCCH TRXs if the following conditions are met: 
1. The uplink receive level after filtering is higher than "Level Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH".
2. The uplink receive quality level after filtering is lower than "Quality Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH". 
3. The Non-BCCH load is higher than "Non-BCCH Load Threshold for TIGHT BCCH HO".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a small value, BCCHs fail to be assigned, decreasing the access success rate.

Parameter Name: Quality Thresh for Assign BCCH Under TBCCH
Meaning:
During channel assignment, the assignment of channels on the BCCH TRXs depends on the uplink receive level, quality, and non-BCCH load. The TCHs are preferentially assigned on the BCCH TRXs if the following conditions are met: 
1. The uplink receive level after filtering is higher than "Level Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH".
2. The uplink receive quality level after filtering is lower than "Quality Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH". 
3. The Non-BCCH load is higher than "Non-BCCH Load Threshold for TIGHT BCCH HO".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If this parameter is set to a large value, BCCHs fail to be assigned, decreasing the access success rate.

Parameter Name: TIGHT BCCH Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the BCCH aggressive frequency reuse algorithm
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Non-BCCH Load Threshold for TIGHT BCCH HO
Meaning:
If the load on the non-BCCH TRX is less than the value of "TIGHTBCCHHOLOADTHRES" when the BSC decides whether to trigger a TIGHT BCCH handover, the BSC does not trigger a handover.
During channel assignment, the assignment of channels on the BCCH TRXs depends on the uplink receive level, quality, and non-BCCH load. The TCHs are preferentially assigned on the BCCH TRXs if the following conditions are met: 
1. The uplink receive level after filtering is higher than "Level Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH". 
2. The uplink receive quality level after filtering is lower than "Quality Thresh. for Assigning Main BCCH Carrier Channel Under TIGHT BCCH". 
3. The Non-BCCH load is higher than "Non-BCCH Load Threshold for TIGHT BCCH HO".
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Cell LAC
Likely KPI Impact: HO / identity (can cause HO fail & drop)
Meaning:
Location area code (LAC). An MS can move freely in a location area with no need of location update. Appropriate division of location areas can effectively lighten the signaling load and improve the call completion rate.
The LAC is a 2-byte hexadecimal code. It ranges from 0000 to FFFF(ffff). The codes 0000 and FFFE(fffe) are reserved. Only the LMT supports hexadecimal codes. The hexadecimal format is H'**** or h'****, for example, H'1214 or h'1214.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Reserved TCH Number for PA Turning On
Meaning: This parameter specifies the number of idle channels that should be reserved on a cell after the TRX is shut down. When the number of idle channels on a cell is less than or equal to this threshold, the BSC enables a TRX. This parameter is used to prevent the impact enabling or disabling delay on the efficiency of channel assignment on the cell that is enabled with the TRX Intelligent Shutdown feature. The value of this parameter represents the number of TCHFs and is used after being converted to the number of TCHHs. For example, if this parameter is set to 1, two idle TCHHs are reserved for the cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Dyn. Turning Off Cell Stop Time
Meaning: End time for dynamically disabling a cell. A cell is not allowed to be disabled from the time specified by this parameter. When the value of "TURNOFFCELLSTPTIME" is less than the value of "TURNOFFCELLSTRTIME", the Dynamic Cell Power Off feature can be enabled for more than a day. When the value of "TURNOFFCELLSTPTIME" is equal to the value of "TURNOFFCELLSTRTIME", the Dynamic Cell Power Off feature can be enabled all day.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Joint Co-Coverage Level Threshold
Meaning: Threshold for determining whether a neighboring cell meets the co-coverage condition. If the level of the neighboring cell is greater than or equal to this threshold in the measurement report, the neighboring cell meets the co-coverage condition.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Joint Co-Coverage Ratio Threshold
Meaning: Threshold for determining whether a serving cell can be disabled. If the proportion of measurement reports indicating that neighboring cells meet the joint co-coverage level threshold condition in all measurement reports is greater than or equal to the value of this parameter, the serving cell can be disabled.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: None

Parameter Name: Low Band Joint Turn-off Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable joint turning-off for a low-band cell. If this parameter is set to ON, the low-band cell (for example, on the 900 MHz band) can be jointly turned off. If this parameter is set to OFF, joint turning-off is not allowed for the low-band cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: Some low-band cells may be shut down if this parameter is set to ON. As a result, the network coverage in the corresponding area may deteriorate, causing traffic volume decrease and deterioration of KPIs such as the paging success rate, access success rate, handover success rate, and call drop rate.

Parameter Name: Preferentially Turn Off BCCH TRX Switch
Meaning: Whether to enable the preferential BCCH TRX shutdown function in the Dynamic Cell Power Off feature. When this parameter is set to ON(On), and conditions for triggering Dynamic Cell Power Off are met, if the BCCH TRX is idle, the BSC preferentially shuts down the BCCH TRX no matter whether other TRXs are occupied. If the BCCH TRX is not idle, the BSC initiates outgoing cell handovers or intra-cell handovers to other TRXs for calls carried on the BCCH TRX and then preferentially shuts down the BCCH TRX. When this parameter is set to OFF(Off), the function does not take effect.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: If the cell outgoing handover success rate is low, setting this parameter to ON(On) increases the immediate assignment success rate, and setting this parameter to OFF(Off) decreases the immediate assignment success rate.

Parameter Name: Same Coverage Cell No
Meaning: Index of a cell that has the same coverage as the current cell.
Impact on Radio Network Performance: The coverage area of co-coverage cells must cover the current cell, which is enabled with the Dynamic Cell Power Off feature. If the planning is incorrect, the current cell may be shut down mistakenly. As a result, the network coverage in the corresponding area may deteriorate, causing traffic volume decrease and deterioration of KPIs such as the paging success rate, access success rate, handover success rate, and call drop rate.

Parameter Name: Enable Turning Off Cell
